task.description: Design a durable, always-current (not periodic-snapshot-based) fix for Letflow.Engine.build_instance_state/3's hardcoded join_counters: %{} (ISS-0397), so a PARALLEL_GATEWAY join can fire across separate complete_task/3 calls, without reintroducing staleness via SnapshotWriter's periodic snapshot table.
acceptance_criteria: Exact persistence mechanism specified: which column/field, when written, when read, under what lock scope relative to complete_task/3's existing M1/M2 lock ordering
Correctness argument proving no new race is introduced, including a concrete two-sibling-branch-completing-in-parallel scenario under real concurrency
Migration specified per this project's conventions (tenant-scoped guard, manifest registration, DB-level default given instance_projections already has live rows)
Test design for a genuine cross-call, concurrent-branch-completion regression test (two separate complete_task/3 calls, real concurrency via Task.async, not one in-memory Transition-only test)
Interaction with ISS-0396 confirmed non-overlapping (independently re-derived, not trusted from ISSUE-FIXER's summary alone)
No implementation code -- signatures/@specs/algorithm-shape descriptions only
Every resolvable question resolved explicitly; anything not resolvable stated as an open question, not silently deferred

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/iss0397-join-counters-fix.md. Fix: add instance_projections.join_counters (:map/jsonb, null: false, default: %{}, same idiom as the existing :variables column) -- no new table, no new lock. Write site: reconcile_projection/5 (engine.ex ~2821, the M10 :projection step), confirmed shared by BOTH complete_task/3's success tail (build_complete_task_tail_multi/6) and advance_after_timer_fired/3's persist_timer_fired_advance/7 -- one function change covers both callers. Read site: build_instance_state/3 (engine.ex ~1813), confirmed by direct read to be the single shared function both build_snapshot_and_state/4 (complete_task/3's M3) and build_snapshot_and_state_for_timer/4 (timer path's M3) call -- reads projection.join_counters off the exact %InstanceProjection{} struct M2's fetch_and_lock_instance_projection/3 already locked earlier in the same transaction, not a second unlocked read. Serialization reuses SnapshotWriter's existing (REQ-054, already-reviewed) join_counter_entry_to_map/from_map codec, promoted from private to two new public functions (SnapshotWriter.serialize_join_counters/1, deserialize_join_counters/1) so Letflow.Engine depends only on the pure map-shape codec, never on SnapshotWriter.latest_snapshot/2 or the periodic instance_state_snapshots table -- explicitly distinguished in the doc from the stale-read anti-pattern ISSUE-FIXER flagged. Correctness argument (design doc section 3): no new lock/no new I/O outside the M2-FOR-UPDATE window complete_task/3 already opens; walked through a concrete real two-Task.async-branch-completion scenario (section 3.3) showing the join fires exactly once regardless of which branch's transaction wins the M2 lock race, via MVCC read-after-lock-release semantics -- explicit non-goal noted that which branch 'wins' is not asserted, only that the outcome is correct either way. Migration spec (section 4): new tenant-scoped migration, add :join_counters, :map, null: false, default: %{} -- explicitly flagged that, unlike the repository_artifacts addendum this migration's style is modeled on, instance_projections already carries live rows in every provisioned tenant, so a real DB-level default is mandatory here, not merely stylistic. Test design (section 5): serial two-call happy path with a regression-locking negative-control note, a genuine concurrent Task.async/Task.await_many two-branch race modeled on engine_cancel_instance_test.exs's own AC4 precedent (Sandbox mode :auto, real separate Postgres connections), a timer-fire parity test (since reconcile_projection/5 is shared), and a narrow SnapshotWriter codec round-trip unit test. ISS-0396 interaction (section 8): independently re-read docs/issues/ISS-0396.yaml (not just ISSUE-FIXER's summary) and confirmed this fix's three touched functions (build_instance_state/3, reconcile_projection/5, SnapshotWriter/InstanceProjection) share zero code with ISS-0396's :task_records Ecto.Multi key-collision defect in the SUB_PROCESS-completion-cascade branch -- safe to land in either order, with a narrow re-verification note if landing order changes build_complete_task_tail_multi/6's step positions. Additional finding surfaced during this design and NOT asked for by the task prompt but load-bearing (section 6): req052-instance-cancellation.md's own design explicitly cites 'the join-counters persistence gap' as its stated reason for NOT wiring {:cancel_branch, _} through cancel_instance/3 -- this fix removes exactly that cited blocker. This design does not change cancel_instance/3's behavior at all (out of scope, confirmed it never calls Transition.transition/3), but flags for REVIEWER/ORCH, per core-directives.md's decision-record-drift rule, that REQ-052's OQ-2 resolution rested on a premise this fix now falsifies -- named explicitly rather than silently left inconsistent or silently re-decided. Two open questions left genuinely open (not resolvable from material read): OQ-2 (whether the codec belongs on SnapshotWriter vs. JoinCounter itself -- a judgment call) and OQ-3 (REQ-048's own pre-existing, unresolved tokens-row-locking OQ-5, restated as still out of this fix's scope, with an explicit argument in section 3.4 that this fix's own correctness proof does not depend on OQ-5 being resolved).
result.routing: Route to Step 2b CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate this design before ELIXIR-DEV implements. Given this issue's flagged comparable rigor bar to ISS-0398 (2 real BLOCKER reworks), the validator should scrutinize section 3's locking/correctness argument and section 2.4/2.5's exact read/write call-site claims against the real code with the same skepticism ISS-0398's validator applied, not accept the walkthrough narrative at face value.
